mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in WORKPLACES combined with a surge in GROCERY_PHARM marks a substitution toward errand-based, non-work trips that also lifts retail visits within one to four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below its prior-2-week mean while GROCERY_PHARM rises above it
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise above its prior 4-week mean within 14 days after WORKPLACES weakens and GROCERY_PHARM strengthens together.

mechanism_narrative: A one-week jump in PARKS indicates discretionary outing intensity that spills into retail and recreation with a short lag, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by at least 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase in the week after PARKS posts a week-on-week rise of 5 points or more.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent collapse in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals a restriction shock or holiday shutdown that suppresses retail traffic over the following month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below 0 and WORKPLACES falls below 0 in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES turn negative together.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained gains in GROCERY_PHARM absorb trip demand into essential shopping and crowd out discretionary retail visits, causing RETAIL_REC to soften over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises rather than falls over the next 28 days during periods when GROCERY_PHARM remains above its recent average.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL rises and TRANSIT simultaneously falls, trips are reallocated to local non-retail activity, reducing retail-and-recreation mobility within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 0 while TRANSIT drops below 0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL turns positive and TRANSIT turns negative in the same week.

mechanism_narrative: A gradual rise in PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM is a warm-weather or holiday pattern that increases overall outing frequency, but the retail lift appears only after a four-week build-up.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both trend upward for at least two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week mean by the end of week 4 after PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both trend upward.

mechanism_narrative: The retail effect is positive only if TRANSIT recovers first; a transit rebound restores access to shopping districts and then lifts RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT turns from negative to positive
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines in the two weeks after TRANSIT crosses from below 0 to above 0.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stay above baseline while RESIDENTIAL stays below baseline, weekday routine activity remains commuter-heavy and retail-and-recreation mobility stays elevated over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not stay above its prior 4-week mean when WORKPLACES remains positive and RESIDENTIAL remains negative for most of the month.
